newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro stocks close at record highs, dlr firm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro stocks close at record highs, dlr firm.

text.p: Stock markets in Britain, France and Germany closed at record highs on Wednesday, helped by the stronger dollar which rose undeterred by a German statement on foreign exchange rates.

The UK's FTSE 100 index faltered on the brink of 5,000 points and eased off the day's best levels to end at a fresh closing high of 4,964.2, up 64.9 points but off the day's best and all-time peak of 4,991.8.
Liquidity, stock shortages and dollar strength were behind the FTSE rise, in which banks accounted for almost half the advance with oils and pharmaceuticals also strongly ahead.
Stock markets in Europe received an extra boost when Wall Street opened higher on benign U.S. June inflation figures.
The Dow Jones Industrial average made an early push across the 8,000 mark, then retreated when Kodak opened lower following the company's release of below-forecast second quarter results.
But the Dow recouped these losses, firming as the technology sector extended its mighty rally. The Nasdaq composite gained 24 points, or 1.57 percent, to 1,566.
The Dow's initial failure to hold above 8,000 dragged European indices off the day's peaks but still encamped on previously unvisited high ground.

French shares ended at a closing high on Wednesday, with strong gains in luxury goods and drinks firm LVMH and semiconductor group SGS-Thomson, but were below an all-time high set earlier in the day. Dealers said the 3,000 level on the CAC 40 index could be tested.
Brokers said the continued strength of the dollar and gains on Wall Street as well as rises on other European markets such as London were supporting the market.

The German IBIS DAX rose well clear of the 4,200-point level on Wednesday, with trade underpinned by the strength of the dollar, trading around 1.7990/97 marks, and the continued advance of the Dow Jones industrials.
Banks and chemical stocks were in favour, and retailer Karstadt was up 20.90 marks at 662 marks on the restructuring outlook despite expectations it may be dropped from the DAX in favour of Adidas.
Austrian shares finished at a record high, powering through the 1,400-point barrier as the firm dollar and low interest rates lured buyers in droves.

"This is a scenario for the bulls -- low interest rates and a strong dollar," said a trader. "The path ahead is clear and the ATX (index) should have little trouble vaulting 1,450 in the present environment."
The dollar, locked in a tight range until the 1230 GMT release of U.S. consumer price data, then gathered strength to rise easily beyond 116 yen and just short of 1.80 marks.
The U.S. Labor Department said June consumer prices rose 0.1 percent after a similar increase in May, interpreted by the market as a tame inflation scenario.
The U.S. currency shrugged off German government comments that there was no need to dramatise the foreign exchange situation.
Government spokesman Peter Hausmann told journalists after a cabinet meeting that Germany remained in close contact with its G7 partners about foreign exchange developments.

"From Germany's point of view there is no reason to dramatise developments," Hausmann said, adding that the mark's current weakness against the dollar and the pound should be seen as a result of the strong economies in the U.S. and Britain.
He said the Group of Seven industrial nations said in February in Berlin that the appreciation of the mark had been fully corrected.
"Together with our G7 partners we are closely observing developments on foreign exchange markets," Hausmann said.
He said that Chancellor Helmut Kohl stressed at the cabinet meeting that the euro should be introduced on time in 1999 and that it would be a strong currency.
He said the government believes speculation ahead of the planned launch of economic and monetary union (EMU) was affecting the foreign exchange markets.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was at 116.27 yen and 1.7980 marks compared with 115.74 yen and 1.8013 marks in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 64.9 points at 4,964.2.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was up 80.11 points at 4,201.24.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 37.31 points at 2,988.01.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at $319.50, unchanged from the morning fixing. Silver was at $4.32, unchanged from the opening.
